description.en: Example Tyre Ontology (ETO) is an exemplar ontology for the tyre sector. It specialises the EU DPP Core Ontology (CORE), whose terms it references by their IRIs.

comments.en: Developed against the CIRPASS-2 CORE ontology as of 12 October 2026: core v2.0.7, P_DPP v2.1.0, IDENT v1.2.0, CON v2.2.0, ACTOR v2.1.3, EVENT v1.0.0, SOC v2.0.0. Checked against the CORE of 21 October 2026: core v2.1.0, P_DPP v2.2.0, IDENT v1.2.0, CON v2.4.0, ACTOR v2.2.0, EVENT v1.0.0, SOC v2.2.0. The CORE is referenced by IRI, without owl:imports: load the CORE files together with this file for reasoning or validation. Terms without dcterms:references were created for this ontology, most of them from non-public data of the CIRPASS-2 tyre pilot.

Tyre is a thick rubber ring, often filled with air, that is fitted around the outer edge of the wheel of a vehicle, allowing the vehicle to stick to the road surface and to travel over the ground more easily [Cambridge Dictionary].

Tyre class C3: tyres designed primarily for heavy-duty vehicles, such as trucks and buses. Value of eudpp:hasProductGroup for a tyre.
Tyre class C2: tyres designed primarily for light commercial vehicles. Value of eudpp:hasProductGroup for a tyre.

comment.undefined: Group of tyre properties corresponding to the EU tyre label and its registration (e.g. wet grip class, EPREL record).

comment.undefined: For commercial tyres, speed adjusted load for dual fitment
Nominal section width of the tyre defined by a code (CV tyre)
Recycling channel category to which the used tyre has been sent (e.g. cement, pyrolysis).
Load capacity index of the tyre when fitted in dual (twin) configuration, as marked on commercial vehicle tyres.

Incremental counter of the retreading operations performed during the tyre's life, starting at zero. The retreader is recorded with an eudpp:ActorRoleAssignment (eudpp:hasActor, eudpp:hasRole eudpp:remanufacturer, eudpp:inContextOfProduct).

It indicates the presence of an internal structure with specific characteristics added to a “conventional” tyre with the aim to reduce the tyre cavity noise (not necessarily external rolling noise) (TRUE/FALSE)
Indicates whether the tyre has been regrooved according to ECE R54 definition

Rim diameter in millimeters or inches
Group of tyre properties describing its technical specification (e.g. load index, speed symbol, structure).

In millimeters, the remaining tread depth of the used tyre at the moment of deconstruction
Date when the ELT has been deconstructed.
URL of an image of the EU tyre label of the tyre.

references.value: Regulation (EU) 2020/740, Annex III (c); UN Regulations No 30 and No 54

comment.undefined: Speed category symbol: letter indicating the maximum speed at which the tyre can carry the load corresponding to its load index (e.g. H = 210 km/h).
An incremental counter to record the number of repairs/patch occurred during the tyre's life - starting with zero

label.undefined: Load Index Dual Fitment After RET

comment.undefined: Load index for dual fitment after Retreading
Load version of the tyre: LL (light load), SL (standard load), XL (extra load) or HL (high load).

references.value: Regulation (EU) 2020/740, Annex III (h); EPREL field iceTyre

comment.undefined: Indication of whether the tyre is an ice grip tyre (true or false).
Group of tyre properties corresponding to markings on the tyre sidewall (e.g. M+S, 3PMSF, size prefix).
Indicates whether an electronic Sensor is present on the tyre updated at each tyre inspection

Scheme of tyre type identifiers: codes, usually alphanumeric, which distinguish a specific tyre type from other tyre types that have the same trade name or the same trademark as that of the supplier. Used with granularity eudpp:model.

Serialised GTIN: a GTIN combined with a serial number, identifying one individual trade item; here in the EPC pure identity URN form (urn:epc:id:sgtin:...). Used with granularity eudpp:item. Local scheme until the CORE IDENT module provides one.

Tire Identification Number required on tyres for the US market: plant code (2 or 3 characters, only 3 from April 2025), tyre size code, optional manufacturer code and date code (week and year of manufacture, WWYY). Used with granularity eudpp:batch.

altLabel.value: European Product Registry for Energy Labelling

comment.undefined: Scheme of the registration numbers that the European Product Registry for Energy Labelling (EPREL) gives to the product models registered by their suppliers. Used with granularity eudpp:model. The public EPREL record URL is built from the number. Local scheme: the CORE IDENT module has no EPREL scheme.
It indicates tubeless or tube type tyres

references.value: Regulation (EU) 2020/740, Annex III (g); UN Regulation No 117

comment.undefined: Three-peak-mountain snowflake (3PMSF) marking: indicates a tyre for use in severe snow conditions.

references.value: Regulation (EU) 2020/740, Annex III (c); UN Regulations No 30 and No 54

comment.undefined: Load capacity index: number associated with the maximum load the tyre can carry at the speed indicated by its speed symbol.

comment.undefined: Tyre size designation as marked on the sidewall (e.g. 195/65 R 17).
Regulation under which the label classes of the tyre (fuel efficiency, wet grip, external rolling noise) are given, e.g. Regulation (EU) 2020/740.
External rolling noise value of the tyre, in decibels (dB), as shown on the EU tyre label.
Code description: lists the regulations with which the tyre is compliant.
Date from which the supplier no longer places the tyre type on the Union market. The first placing on the market is recorded with a eudpp:PlacingOnMarketEvent.
Whether the tyre type is available in all EU and EEA countries. If not, eto:availableInCountry gives the countries where it is available.
Two-letter code of a country where the tyre type is available, as in EPREL: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, except EL for Greece and XI for Northern Ireland. One value per country.

references.value: Regulation (EU) 2020/740, Annex III (i); EPREL fields dateStartProductionWeek and dateStartProductionYear

comment.undefined: Week and year in which the production of the tyre type started, written as an ISO 8601 week (e.g. 2021-W10). The regulation gives two digits for the week and two digits for the year.
Long commercial description of the tyre, combining its size, service description and commercial name (e.g. 195/65 R 17 87H Dakota Spring).

comment.undefined: Week and year in which the production of the tyre type ended, once known, written as an ISO 8601 week (e.g. 2025-W52).
